question: In the pulverized-coal boiler co-firing ammonia, why did NO emissions keep rising all the way up to 80% NH3 blending?
expect: premise false: NO rose from 20% to 60% but DECREASED at 80% (H/OH radical competition) (abstract)
rendered:
The document does not explicitly state why NO emissions kept rising all the way up to 80% NH3 blending. However, it does mention that the NO emission trend is nonlinear and that the NO peak shifts downstream as the NH3 blending ratio increases. 

The document suggests that at high NH3 fractions, NH3 dehydrogenation depletes H/OH radicals, promotes N2 formation via NHi, and suppresses NO production. However, it also mentions that at 80% NH3 blending, the required ignition energy becomes sufficiently high that no combustion is observed in the flame zone, and the main heat release shifts downstream to the post flame zone. This might contribute to the non-linear increase in NO emissions.
